name: Doutai
catalog_quote: 3.1 STRESS — Stress, often manifested by length, is found on the first syllable of the word. As such, it is not emic.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding sentence is verbatim at McAllister & McAllister 1991:134 in the held SIL PDF (PDF p. 21), and the Hartzler afterword caveat is verbatim at pp. 141-142. (2) Deciding source: a 1991 SIL field phonology article, the only description of Doutai in existence per Glottolog (1 descriptive ref) and the SIL archive (1 item for tds); Clouse 1997 (held) independently states stress is non-contrastive across Lakes Plain and defers to McAllister for Doutai. No reference grammar, dissertation, JIPA illustration or instrumental study was found in any bibliography opened; the language is moribund (~335 speakers in 1991). (3) Wishlist: empty — nothing unheld is known to exist. sources.quote: "3.1 STRESS — Stress, often manifested by length, is found on the first syllable of the word. As such, it is not emic." (p. 134). Supporting, editor's afterword p. 142: "A change in this position was forced when an across-the-board first syllable stress analysis was adopted. ... Further investigation, in fact, may well reveal factors which will either disprove the stress rule, or give clues to the assimilation of these apparently paradoxical factors."
